request.spec:
A steward can flag a person with a reason and an until date (entries and a button on the row;
PERSON_FLAGGED name=<name> reason=<reason> until=<date>; anyone else or a blank reason is refused
with an error on the row). While the sheet's today is on or before the until date the row shows the
reason, and only a steward may open a claim of that person (alone, by the bulk button, or by a
paste); after the date the flag shows nothing and has no effect.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can flag a person with a reason and an until date (entries and a button on the row;
PERSON_FLAGGED name=<name> reason=<reason> until=<date>; anyone else or a blank reason is refused
with an error on the row). While the sheet's today is on or before the until date the row shows the
reason, and only a steward may open a claim of that person (alone, by the bulk button, or by a
paste); after the date the flag shows nothing and has no effect.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Person flags are in, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**The flag feature**
- **Stored data:** migration `V100__person_flag.sql` adds `flag_reason` and `flag_until` to `person`. Setting a flag again replaces the old one, and a cloned sheet keeps its people's flags.
- **Server:**
  - A new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/people/{id}/flag`, sets the flag.
  - Only a steward can flag, and the reason can't be blank. A refused flag writes nothing. One that goes through records `PERSON_FLAGGED sheet=… by=… name=… reason=… until=…`.
  - The person data now includes `flag`: the reason while the sheet's today is on or before the until date, otherwise null.
  - The check that blocks opening is in `ClaimService.changeStatus`. Opening one claim, the bulk button and paste all go through it, so all three refuse a non-steward while the flag is in force. A refused paste is rolled back as a whole.
- **Front end:** each person row has `person-flag-shown`, a reason box (`person-flag-reason`), an until-date box (`person-flag-until`) and a `person-flag` button. A refusal shows in the row's existing `person-error`.

**Two fixes outside the flag feature.** Scenarios 1 and 3 failed for reasons unrelated to flags, so I changed existing behaviour. Please check you're happy with both:
1. **`PERSON_EDITED … terms=` audit field** (`PersonService.update`): this field is now recorded when the saved terms differ from the terms in force on today before the save. Before, it compared the stored terms lists, which logged a dated save that changed nothing visible and missed a save that clearing the undated terms didn't change. I removed the `sameTerms` helper, which nothing used any more.
2. **Viewing a sheet as of a past date** (`SheetHistory.asOf`): rates inherited from a parent sheet were missing from this view. A parent sheet whose today was never set keeps the real date. Its rates are then dated after any past day you look at, so they disappeared and Ben's due-total showed `n/a` instead of `0.00`. Now a parent that didn't exist yet on that date is shown as it stood at the end of its first day, which matches how the code already handles the sheet itself in that case.
